title: Inventory oversells during a flash sale

hints.title: Where to look
hints.body: Focus on `handlePurchase` in `src/charge.js`. Notice that it performs three distinct async steps: read stock → check quantity → decrement. Add some print statements or mentally trace what happens when 5 requests all execute the read step before any of them executes the decrement.

hints.title: The concept
hints.body: This is a **TOCTOU (Time-of-Check to Time-of-Use) race condition**. Between the `findUnique` (read) and the `update` (write), another concurrent request can also read the same positive quantity and pass the check — so both decrement, potentially pushing stock below zero. The fix requires making the read and write **atomic**.

hints.title: The fix approach
hints.body: Wrap the entire read-check-write in `db.$transaction(async (tx) => { ... })`. Inside the transaction callback, use `tx.stock.findUnique` and `tx.stock.update` — the in-memory stub serialises execution inside a transaction so there is no yield between operations. On a real Postgres database this corresponds to `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` inside a transaction, or an atomic conditional `UPDATE stock SET quantity = quantity - 1 WHERE productId = $1 AND quantity > 0` checking rows-affected. Throw with a `.status` property to signal 404 / 409 from inside the transaction.

badPatches.title: Double-Check Without Transaction Locking
badPatches.summary: 60/100 — passes visible tests (60/60), fails H1 and H2 (concurrent inventory oversell)
